Idiopathic Retroperitoneal Fibrosis: The patient's presentation of asymptomatic left-sided hydronephrosis, ill-defined fascial planes around the kidney, and thickening around the renal hilum, along with the microscopic examination showing hypocellular interweaving thick collagen bundles with extensive hyalination and bland spindle cells, are consistent with Idiopathic Retroperitoneal Fibrosis. The patient's ureteral obstruction and renal failure also support this diagnosis.
Retroperitoneal Fibrosis: The patient's presentation of abdominal pain, ill-defined fascial planes around the kidney, and thickening around the renal hilum, along with the microscopic examination showing hypocellular interweaving thick collagen bundles with extensive hyalination and bland spindle cells, are consistent with Retroperitoneal Fibrosis. The patient's inflammatory cells, including lymphocytes, eosinophils, and plasma cells, also support this diagnosis.
